subject: Request: Keystone runtime capacity - approval to add 3 infra roles
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Keystone runtime capacity - approval to add 3 infra roles

Team,

TL;DR: Requesting expedited approval to add 3 headcount seats to the runtime/infra slate for Q3: 1 Senior Kernel Engineer, 1 Platform SRE, and 1 Production Runtime Engineer (quant/latency focus). These are critical to deliver the low-latency rollout for our new compaction scheduler and the EU region capacity ramp.

Why now:
- Observability indicates persistent tail latency on long-context workloads; kernel optimizations require a dedicated senior engineer to own prioritization and release windows.
- Upcoming EU region capacity ramp (+30% traffic) needs an SRE to own GPUS pool autoscaling policy and on-call.
- We have a contractor covering parts of the production runtime work; converting that work into an FTE will yield better continuity and reduce cross-team handoffs.

What I’m asking:
- Approval to open 3 reqs (headcount) and permission to offer up to the listed comp bands in the attached PDF.
- Budget: $540k run-rate fully loaded (see impact_matrix.xlsx) — this includes salary + benefits + hiring overhead.
- Decision timeline: Need a go/no-go by EOD next Wednesday (2026-07-21) to hit recruiting lead times for an August start.

Attachments: headcount_request_q3_v2.pdf, impact_matrix.xlsx

Proposed next steps:
1) Kimberly: confirmation on comp band tolerance and whether we need exec approval for the Senior Kernel band.
2) Marcus: confirm budget re-allocation or note if this needs finance sign-off.
3) Soojin: if approved, we’ll fast-track with Talent Partners (Emily) and aim for 3-week on-site slate.

Open points I expect to land in our decision: whether a contractor backfill is acceptable as a temporary measure, and whether we must cap offers to the mid of the band or can go to top-of-band for exceptional candidates.

Thanks — I know this is fast, but this is in the critical path for the scheduler launch.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Director, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Park <emily.park@talentpartners.io>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 11:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Keystone runtime capacity - approval to add 3 infra roles

Logan — thanks for the concise ask. A couple of quick clarifying questions before I sign off: 

- Comp bands: the senior kernel band you listed sits above our pre-approved non-exec cap. We need either a compensation exception (if we go to top-of-band) or explicit signoff that we stay at band midpoint. Please confirm your recommendation and whether you have benchmarked against similar hires (Marcus, can you confirm budget headroom?).

- Backfill: if we convert the contractor to an FTE, do we expect an overlap period where we pay both? How many weeks? Please add the contractor name and current weekly rate to the impact matrix so finance can model.

- Can Emily share a short candidate pipeline and expected time-to-offer? If the pipeline is shallow, we should consider an external agency bump.

If we can get those answers today I can route to Finance for an expedited review.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
VP, People & GTM Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Emily Park <emily.park@talentpartners.io>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 08:47:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Keystone runtime capacity - approval to add 3 infra roles

Hi all — sharing a short update from Talent Partners. Attached is a short-list with current market feedback (candidate_shortlist.pdf). High-level notes: 

- Senior Kernel Engineer: we currently have two pre-screened candidates with kernel-level experience on aten/torch kernels and production quantization work. Expected offer window: 10-14 days once we have permission to make offers. Market velocity is fast; to secure either candidate we recommend offering to top-of-band (justification: niche skill set).

- Platform SRE: three available candidates with solid cloud-native infra backgrounds. Mid-of-band should be competitive in our target regions (US-West). Can accept below top-of-band if we can promise on-call rotation minimization.

- Production Runtime Engineer (contractor conversion): contractor (John S.) is willing to convert, expects 10% uplift on current contractor comp. If you approve conversion we can lock him with a sign-on and a 4-week overlap for knowledge transfer.

Attachments: candidate_shortlist.pdf (includes linked refs and expected offer ranges).

Let me know if you want Talent Partners to run a parallel market search for the kernel role; we can deploy a seeding campaign within 48 hours.

Best,
Emily Park
Senior Recruiter, Talent Partners
em: emily.park@talentpartners.io

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Keystone runtime capacity - approval to add 3 infra roles

Kim, Logan — after reviewing the impact_matrix and the notes from Emily, I’m providing conditional approval for the 3 headcount requests. Conditions below: 

1) Contractor conversion for John S. is approved as an FTE with a one-time 4-week overlap. Finance will cover overlap from the Q3 hiring buffer; no additional reallocations required.
2) Senior Kernel hire: allow offers up to the top-of-band only if the candidate passes a technical interview panel (kernel + quant + systems) and we document the scarcity case in the offer memo. If we cannot find a strong match within 3 weeks we revert to a focused external search budget.

Please proceed to open the reqs with Talent Partners and share offer approvals under the usual 24-hour exec review queue. Emily — please proceed with offers where appropriate after the panel.
